---
title: Formatting
description: >
  Format documents with Panache and see how it lays out Markdown, tables, math,
  and code.
---

Panache formats Markdown source to make it easy to read and consistent across a
project. It preserves the meaning of your document, and running it again on an
already formatted document produces the same output.

## Using the Formatter

### Format and Check Files

Format a document in place, or pass a directory to format its supported files:

```sh
panache format document.qmd
panache format docs/
```

To check formatting without writing changes:

```sh
panache format --check .
```

The command exits with a nonzero status when files need formatting. Both modes
follow the project's configuration and file exclusions. See
[Configuration](configure.qmd).

To read from standard input and write the result to standard output, supply a
filename so Panache can select the document's flavor:

```sh
panache --stdin-filename=document.qmd format <document.qmd
```

See [Editor Setup](lsp.qmd) for formatting while editing and
[Integrations](integrations.qmd) for CI, pre-commit, and dprint.

### Choose a Wrapping Mode

By default, Panache reflows paragraphs to a line width of 80 columns. Put your
project's preferences in `panache.toml`:

```toml
[format]
line-width = 80
wrap = "reflow"
```

Choose a wrapping mode to suit how you write:

  | Mode       | Behavior                                              |
  | ---------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
  | `reflow`   | Rewrap paragraphs to fit `line-width`.                |
  | `preserve` | Keep existing line breaks.                            |
  | `sentence` | Put each sentence on its own line.                    |
  | `semantic` | Keep line breaks and add a break after each sentence. |

`sentence` and `semantic` do not limit line length. Sentence detection accounts
for common abbreviations and the document's language. See [Sentence-Wrapping
Abbreviations](../reference/configuration.qmd#no-break-abbreviations) to
customize the abbreviations.

For a single run, you can override a setting on the command line:

```sh
panache format -o wrap=sentence document.qmd
```

The [configuration reference](../reference/configuration.qmd#formatting-style)
lists all formatting options and their defaults.

### Format Embedded Code

Panache formats code fences and their attributes. To format the code inside
those fences, configure an external formatter and make it available on `PATH`.
See [Configure Linting and Embedded
Code](configure.qmd#configure-linting-and-embedded-code) for setup and the
[formatter presets](../reference/formatter-presets.qmd) for supported tools.

### Ignore Directives

Use HTML comments to preserve a region's formatting. This is useful for ASCII
diagrams or other content whose spacing matters:

```markdown
<!-- panache-ignore-format-start -->
This    paragraph   has    custom     spacing
that  will   be   preserved   exactly.
<!-- panache-ignore-format-end -->
```

To disable both formatting and linting for a region, use
`<!-- panache-ignore-start -->` and `<!-- panache-ignore-end -->` instead.

## Formatting Examples

The examples below show Panache's default formatting for Quarto documents,
unless another setting or flavor is specified. The aim is readable source:
consistent markers, clear indentation, and spacing that makes the document's
structure visible. Some constructs, such as definition lists and fenced divs,
are available only in [flavors](../reference/configuration.qmd#flavor) that
support them.

### Text Wrapping

Paragraphs wrap to `line-width`. With `line-width = 60`:

Input

:   ```markdown
    Panache wraps paragraphs to make the source easier to read and keeps related words together. You can choose a different wrapping mode for your project.
    ```

Output

:   ```markdown
    Panache wraps paragraphs to make the source easier to read
    and keeps related words together. You can choose a different
    wrapping mode for your project.
    ```

Panache preserves hard line breaks in every wrapping mode. It writes them as a
backslash at the end of the line, which is easier to see than two trailing
spaces.

### Headings

Panache uses ATX headings (`#`, `##`, and so on), removes decorative closing
hashes, and adds blank lines around headings. It separates attribute entries
with a single space.

Input

:   ```markdown
    Introduction
    ============
    Text

    ##  Results  ##

    ### Details{.important  .highlight }
    ```

Output

:   ```markdown
    # Introduction

    Text

    ## Results

    ### Details {.important .highlight}
    ```

### Emphasis and Strong

Panache uses asterisks for emphasis and strong emphasis:

Input

:   ```markdown
    An _important_ point and a __strong__ claim.
    ```

Output

:   ```markdown
    An *important* point and a **strong** claim.
    ```

Panache may escape literal emphasis markers so they remain text when the
document is parsed again.

### Code

Panache chooses enough backticks to enclose inline code. Code blocks use
backtick fences, with the language first and any remaining attributes in braces.
Indented code blocks become fenced blocks.

Input

:   ````markdown
    ``` {.haskell .numberLines}
    qsort [] = []
    ```
    ````

Output

:   ````markdown
    ```haskell {.numberLines}
    qsort [] = []
    ```
    ````

Tabs become spaces by default. To keep tabs in code, set
[`tab-stops = "preserve"`](../reference/configuration.qmd#tab-stops).

### Lists

Bullet lists use `-` and two spaces of indentation per level. Panache removes
blank lines between items when each item contains only a single paragraph.

Input

:   ```markdown
    * Item 1
      + Nested item
          *  Deeply nested
     +  Item 2
    ```

Output

:   ```markdown
    - Item 1
      - Nested item
        - Deeply nested
    - Item 2
    ```

Panache preserves the numbering style of ordered and fancy lists and aligns
continuation text with the item text. Task lists use `- [ ]` and `- [x]` for
both top-level and nested tasks. For parsers that require four spaces of
indentation per nesting level, enable the
[`four-space-rule`](../reference/configuration.qmd#lists) extension.

#### Definition Lists

Definition markers use three spaces after `:`. Definitions with several blocks
have blank lines between them, and continuation blocks are indented four spaces.

Input

:   ```markdown
    Term
    : Definition
    ```

Output

:   ```markdown
    Term
    :   Definition
    ```

### Block Quotes

Each line in a block quote starts with `>`, followed by a space. Paragraphs
inside the quote follow the chosen wrapping mode.

Panache preserves the blank line between a list and a following block quote. To
place a quote inside a list item, indent its `>` markers to align with the
item's text.

Input

:   ```markdown
    >This is a block quote. This
    >paragraph has two lines.
    ```

Output

:   ```markdown
    > This is a block quote. This paragraph has two lines.
    ```

### Tables

Panache formats pipe, grid, simple, and multiline tables. By default, it indents
pipe, simple, and multiline tables by two spaces. Set
[`table-indent = 0`](../reference/configuration.qmd#table-indentation) to keep
them at the left margin. Grid tables stay at the left margin so Pandoc
recognizes them as tables.

#### Pipe Tables

Panache pads cells to show each column's alignment in the source. In
Pandoc-based flavors, Panache preserves separator widths when they control the
rendered column proportions.

Input

:   ```markdown
    | Right | Left | Default | Center|
    |------:|:-----|---------|:------:|
    | 12  |  12  |    12   |    12  |
    |  123  |  123 |   123   |   123  |
    |  1  |    1 |     1   |     1 |
    ```

Output

:   ```markdown
      | Right | Left | Default | Center |
      | ----: | :--- | ------- | :----: |
      |    12 | 12   | 12      |   12   |
      |   123 | 123  | 123     |  123   |
      |     1 | 1    | 1       |   1    |
    ```

#### Grid Tables

Panache wraps prose within the existing columns. It keeps column widths because
Pandoc uses them to determine the rendered layout. Lists, code, and other block
content inside cells keep their structure.

Input

:   ```markdown
    +--------------------+--------+
    | Description        | Value  |
    +====================+========+
    | First              | 12     |
    | sample.            |        |
    |                    |        |
    +--------------------+--------+
    ```

Output

:   ```markdown
    +--------------------+--------+
    | Description        | Value  |
    +====================+========+
    | First sample.      | 12     |
    +--------------------+--------+
    ```

#### Simple Tables

Panache sizes columns to fit their contents and aligns cell text according to
the header. It moves captions below the table and prefixes them with `:`.

Input

:   ```markdown
       Right     Left     Center     Default
     -------     ------ ----------   ---------------
          12       12      12            12
       123       123       123          123
           1     1        1             1

       :  A caption
    ```

Output

:   ```markdown
        Right Left    Center  Default
      ------- ------ -------- ---------
           12 12        12    12
          123 123      123    123
            1 1         1     1

      : A caption
    ```

#### Multiline Tables

Panache wraps prose within the existing column widths and removes extra blank
lines between rows. It keeps the widths because they affect the rendered layout.
Code spans, links, and math stay intact when cells wrap.

Input

:   ```markdown
    -------------------------------------------------------------
     Centered   Default           Right Left
      Header    Aligned         Aligned Aligned
    ----------- ------- --------------- -------------------------
      First     row              12.0   Example of a row that
                                        spans multiple lines.


      Second    row                 5.0 Here's another one. Note
                                        the blank line between
                                        rows.
    -------------------------------------------------------------
    ```

Output

:   ```markdown
      -------------------------------------------------------------
       Centered   Default           Right Left
        Header    Aligned         Aligned Aligned
      ----------- ------- --------------- -------------------------
         First    row                12.0 Example of a row that
                                          spans multiple lines.

        Second    row                 5.0 Here's another one. Note
                                          the blank line between
                                          rows.
      -------------------------------------------------------------
    ```

### Math

Panache adds spaces around operators and keeps subscripts and superscripts
tight. In display math, it indents environment bodies and aligns `&` columns and
row endings so the source is easier to follow.

Input

:   ```markdown
    $$
    \begin{aligned}
    x _1&=a+b\\
    x _{12}&=2a+b\\
    y&=a-b
    \end{aligned}
    $$
    ```

Output

:   ```markdown
    $$
      \begin{aligned}
        x_1    & = a + b  \\
        x_{12} & = 2a + b \\
        y      & = a - b
      \end{aligned}
    $$
    ```

By default, long display equations wrap at relations and operators to fit
`line-width`. Content after a multiline environment starts on a new line at the
display indent, with scripts and punctuation attached to the closing marker. Use
`math = "preserve"` to keep your line breaks, or `math = "verbatim"` to leave
the math content untouched. Panache leaves malformed math and command arguments
it cannot interpret unchanged. See [Math
Formatting](../reference/configuration.qmd#math-formatting) for modes, delimiter
styles, and indentation settings.

### Links

Link text and destinations are preserved. Panache normalizes spacing and quotes
around titles and attributes.

Input

:   ```markdown
    [Panache](https://panache.bz/  'Project website')
    ```

Output

:   ```markdown
    [Panache](https://panache.bz/ "Project website")
    ```

### Fenced Divs

Panache normalizes attributes and removes blank lines at the start and end of
the body. Nested divs use two more colons than their parent, making their
boundaries easy to distinguish.

Input

:   ```markdown
    ::: Warning ::::::
    This is a warning.

    ::: Danger
    This is a warning within a warning.
    :::
    ::::::::::::::::::
    ```

Output

:   ```markdown
    ::: Warning
    This is a warning.

    ::::: Danger
    This is a warning within a warning.
    :::::
    :::
    ```

### MyST Directives

In the MyST flavor, Panache normalizes directive options and separates them from
the body with a blank line. It formats prose in directive bodies but preserves
literal content, such as code and math. It also keeps each `toctree` entry on
its own line.

Input

:   ````markdown
    ```{{code-block}} python
    :caption:   Fibonacci

    def fib(n):
        if n < 2:
            return n
        return fib(n - 1) + fib(n - 2)
    ```
    ````

Output

:   ````markdown
    ```{{code-block}} python
    :caption: Fibonacci

    def fib(n):
        if n < 2:
            return n
        return fib(n - 1) + fib(n - 2)
    ```
    ````

### Admonitions

Enable
[`python-markdown-admonitions`](../reference/configuration.qmd#admonitions) to
format `!!!` admonitions and `pymdownx-details` to format collapsible `???` and
`???+` blocks. Panache indents the body by four spaces and formats it like
ordinary content.

Input

:   ```markdown
    !!! note "Heads up"

        Read the introduction
        before running the examples.
    ```

Output

:   ```markdown
    !!! note "Heads up"
        Read the introduction before running the examples.
    ```

### Footnotes

Footnote text follows the chosen wrapping mode. Continuation blocks are indented
four spaces, as in list items.

Input

:   ```markdown
    A claim.[^note]

    [^note]: Supporting evidence appears
        in the appendix.
    ```

Output

:   ```markdown
    A claim.[^note]

    [^note]: Supporting evidence appears in the appendix.
    ```

### Horizontal Rules {#horizontal-rulers}

Horizontal rules use hyphens and extend to `line-width`, making section breaks
visible in the source. With `line-width = 40`:

Input

:   ```markdown
    First section.

    ***

    Second section.
    ```

Output

:   ```markdown
    First section.

    ----------------------------------------

    Second section.
    ```

Set `horizontal-rule-style = "compact"` to use `---` instead. Panache adds blank
lines around rules to keep them distinct from heading underlines and metadata
delimiters.

### Blank Lines

Panache reduces multiple blank lines between blocks to one:

Input

:   ```markdown
    Paragraph 1


    Paragraph 2
    ```

Output

:   ```markdown
    Paragraph 1

    Paragraph 2
    ```

### Frontmatter

Panache normalizes YAML spacing and indentation. Prose in plain and folded (`>`)
scalars follows the document's wrapping mode; literal (`|`) scalars keep their
line breaks.

Input

:   ```markdown
    ---
    echo:    false
    list:
    -  a
    -     b
    ---
    Text
    ```

Output

:   ```markdown
    ---
    echo: false
    list:
      - a
      - b
    ---

    Text
    ```

### Chunk Options

For Quarto and R Markdown code chunks, Panache converts simple header options to
`#|` comments and formats them as YAML. Options containing R expressions stay in
the header.

Input

:   ````markdown
    ```{{r foobar, echo=FALSE, dependson = c("foo", "bar"), fig.cap = "A caption"}}
    a <- 1
    b <- 2
    ```
    ````

Output

:   ````markdown
    ```{{r, dependson=c("foo", "bar")}}
    #| label: foobar
    #| echo: false
    #| fig-cap: "A caption"

    a <- 1
    b <- 2
    ```
    ````

Captions follow the document's wrapping mode. Use a folded scalar (`>-`) for a
long caption that should wrap across lines.
